intro: Lesson 17. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍۢ وَتَبَّ (١) مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ (٢)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained.

keywords.def: an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ who fought Islam

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Masad 111:1-2 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 111:1-2 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Tell a friend one thing that really helps us: our money, or our good deeds?

questions.a: A) Abu Lahab. 111:1 names Abu Lahab.

questions.q: Al-Masad 111:1: «تَبَّتْ يَدَآ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's ﷺ own uncle, yet he hurt him and Islam. Does being family make someone good?
questions.a: No: what matters is belief and good deeds. His money and work did not help him (111:2).
